text:
Ava Li: uploaded a compact mock for Settings with an "error chip" banner that floats above the form instead of a full summary panel. idea: show "2 errors" chip that expands inline to reveal linked field errors. Devin Park: I like the chip for density. question: should field errors appear on blur or only after first submit? inline-on-blur helps catch typos but can feel noisy. Renee S.: prefer hybrid: show inline on blur for required fields, but avoid validation for optional fields until submit. we also need consistent placement of helper text vs error text to avoid layout jumps. Omar H: accessibility reminder: expanded chip must receive focus and be announced. consider aria-live="polite" for blur-time hints, but use aria-live="assertive" on submit to make sure screen readers notify the summary. also add aria-controls pointing to a list of links that move focus to inputs. Priya Rao: copy proposal for chip states: - collapsed: "2 problems — expand" - expanded: "We couldn't save. Fix the highlighted fields or press Esc to dismiss." For deletes: keep language explicit about consequences and avoid euphemisms. Ava Li: destructive flow options: 1) inline confirm toggle + undo snackbar for single item; 2) modal with checkbox + typed-name for multi-item or irreversible deletes. prefer using typed-name only when there is no server-side undo. Devin Park: mobile constraint: chip should be sticky at the top of the viewport once visible, but collapse to a banner bar to save vertical space. make sure it doesn't obscure form controls. Renee S.: UI detail: error text baseline should align with helper text so rows don't jump. we can reserve space for potential errors or animate height change. Omar H: sample markup suggestion: ```

``` Omar H: when expanding, move focus into the chip and trap keyboard until user presses Esc or chooses a link. ensure screen readers announce number of errors. Priya Rao: for required indicators, I'm leaning to a visible pale pill that says "Required" for dense tables, and the standard asterisk for single-line forms. but always provide a sr-only text that reads "required" after the label for assistive tech. Ava Li: next steps: I'll prototype three variants: chip-collapsed (sticky), chip-expanded (inline list + linked anchors), and modal-typed confirm for irreversible deletes. will include copies and the accessibility pattern. design-bot: Created design doc: https://redwood/designs/error-chip-patterns 3 accessibility checklist and metrics (error correction rate, accidental delete incidents). Devin Park: i'll do mobile breakpoints and share an animated prototype. Renee S.: looping in UX Writing @Priya for final microcopy choices. Ava Li: thanks all 3 please react which variant you prefer so i can move to dev handoff.
